## Overview

This vignette reproduces the core analyses of the CATALYST/CyTOF differential
discovery workflow -- Nowicka *et al.* 2017/2019, *"CyTOF workflow:
differential discovery in high-throughput high-dimensional cytometry
datasets"*, F1000Research 6:748 (a copy of the v4 manuscript is included at
`vignettes/support/`) -- on the same public PBMC/BCR-XL dataset (Bodenmiller
*et al.* 2012), using the reference implementation (`CATALYST` + `diffcyt` +
`ConsensusClusterPlus`), and then shows the same clustering inside **CySA**.

Every code chunk below was run against the actually installed package
versions and the real dataset before being written down (not merely
transcribed from the paper); two real incompatibilities between the 2019
paper's code and current Bioconductor releases were found and are called out
where they occur. This is not a Bioconductor-submission vignette (it depends
on `HDCytoData`/`ExperimentHub` downloads and takes a couple of minutes to
run); see the note at the end on how it is packaged.

We use the exact parameters the paper specifies:

- arcsinh transformation with **cofactor 5** for all channels (the CyTOF
  standard; `CATALYST::prepData()`'s own default),
- FlowSOM grid **10 x 10** (100 codes), `ConsensusClusterPlus` **maxK = 20**,
  **seed = 1234**,
- 10 lineage ("type") markers for clustering, 14 functional/signaling
  ("state") markers for differential-state analysis.

```{r libs}
library(HDCytoData)
library(CATALYST)
library(diffcyt)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(S4Vectors)
library(CySA)
```

## Data import

`HDCytoData::Bodenmiller_BCR_XL_SE()` gives the same 8-donor,
Reference-vs-BCR/FcR-XL subset the paper uses (originally downloadable from
the Robinson Lab server / Citrus Cytobank repository as raw FCS files). Its
layout needs a bit of care: unlike a typical
`SingleCellExperiment`/`SummarizedExperiment`, HDCytoData's `_SE()` objects
store **rows = cells, columns = markers**, with *marker* metadata
(`channel_name`, `marker_name`, `marker_class`) in `colData()` and *per-cell*
metadata (`sample_id`, `group_id`, `patient_id`) in `rowData()` -- the
opposite of the usual convention.

```{r import}
se <- Bodenmiller_BCR_XL_SE()
dim(se)

## Marker metadata (one row per channel) and per-cell metadata (one row
## per cell) -- note the "reversed" accessors for this object.
marker_meta <- as.data.frame(colData(se))
cell_meta <- as.data.frame(rowData(se))
table(marker_meta$marker_class)
table(cell_meta$group_id)
```

`CATALYST::prepData()` expects a `flowSet` (one `flowFrame` per sample). We
build one directly from the assay matrix, splitting rows by
`cell_meta$sample_id`:

```{r build-flowset}
raw <- assay(se, "exprs")  # cells x channels, RAW (untransformed) intensities
## ?Bodenmiller_BCR_XL_SE confirms these are raw ion counts and should be
## arcsinh-transformed (cofactor 5) before use -- prepData() does this below.

split_idx <- split(seq_len(nrow(raw)), cell_meta$sample_id)
ffs <- lapply(names(split_idx), function(fn) {
    m <- raw[split_idx[[fn]], , drop = FALSE]
    storage.mode(m) <- "double"
    flowCore::flowFrame(m)
})
names(ffs) <- names(split_idx)
fs <- methods::as(ffs, "flowSet")
flowCore::sampleNames(fs) <- names(ffs)
```

`panel` and `md` mirror the paper's `PBMC8_panel_v3.xlsx` /
`PBMC8_metadata.xlsx` structure, built directly from the SE's own metadata
instead of downloading external spreadsheets:

```{r panel-md}
panel <- marker_meta
panel$antigen <- panel$marker_name

md <- unique(cell_meta[, c("sample_id", "group_id", "patient_id")])
md$condition <- factor(ifelse(md$group_id == "Reference", "Ref", "BCRXL"),
    levels = c("Ref", "BCRXL"))
md$sample_id <- factor(
    paste0(md$condition, match(md$patient_id, unique(md$patient_id))),
    levels = paste0(rep(c("Ref", "BCRXL"), each = 8), rep(1:8, 2))
)
md$file_name <- names(split_idx)
md <- md[match(names(split_idx), md$file_name), ]
```

**Gotcha found while building this (not in the paper):** `panel$fcs_colname`
/ the flowSet's column names must be the **isotope-tagged channel names**
(e.g. `"pNFkB(Nd142)Dd"`), not the plain antigen name (`"pNFkB"`).
`CATALYST::prepData()` decides whether a channel is a real mass-cytometry
channel with `as.numeric(gsub("[[:punct:][:alpha:]]", "", chs))`: it strips
all letters and punctuation and treats a channel as "non-mass" (like `Time`)
if nothing but digits remain. Plain antigen names that happen to contain a
digit (`CD3`, `pS6`, ...) survive this test by accident; those that don't
(`pNFkB`, `pAkt`, `pBtk`, `pErk`, `pLat`, `IgM`, `HLA-DR` -- 7 of the 24
markers) get silently dropped from the assay. Using `channel_name` (which
always contains the isotope mass number) avoids this entirely:

```{r fix-channel-names}
colnames(raw) <- panel$channel_name       # rebuild with the isotope-tagged names
panel$fcs_colname <- panel$channel_name
ffs <- lapply(names(split_idx), function(fn) {
    m <- raw[split_idx[[fn]], , drop = FALSE]
    storage.mode(m) <- "double"
    flowCore::flowFrame(m)
})
names(ffs) <- names(split_idx)
fs <- methods::as(ffs, "flowSet")
flowCore::sampleNames(fs) <- names(ffs)
```

```{r prepdata}
sce <- prepData(fs, panel, md, features = panel$fcs_colname)
sce
length(type_markers(sce))   # 10, as expected
length(state_markers(sce))  # 14, as expected
```

**Sanity check against the paper's Figure 2:** the per-sample cell counts
should match exactly, since this is the identical published subset.

```{r fig2-check}
n_cells(sce)
```

Reference cell counts from the paper (Figure 2): Ref1-8 = 2739, 16725, 9434,
6906, 11962, 11038, 15974, 13670; BCRXL1-8 = 2838, 16675, 12252, 8990, 8543,
8622, 14770, 11653. They match.

## Diagnostic plots

```{r plotCounts}
plotCounts(sce, color_by = "condition")
```

```{r plotExprs, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
p <- CATALYST::plotExprs(sce, color_by = "condition")
p$facet$params$ncol <- 6
p
```

**MDS plot.** The paper's `CATALYST::plotMDS()` was renamed to `pbMDS()`
(pseudobulk MDS) in current CATALYST:

```{r pbMDS}
CATALYST::pbMDS(sce, color_by = "condition")
```

**Figure 4 equivalent** -- heatmap of median (arcsinh-transformed) marker
expression of all 24 markers per sample:

```{r fig4}
CATALYST::plotExprHeatmap(sce, bin_anno = TRUE, row_anno = TRUE)
```

**Figure 5 equivalent** -- non-redundancy scores of the 10 lineage markers:

```{r fig5}
plotNRS(sce, features = type_markers(sce), color_by = "condition")
```

## Clustering: FlowSOM + ConsensusClusterPlus

```{r cluster}
set.seed(1234)
sce <- cluster(sce, features = type_markers(sce),
    xdim = 10, ydim = 10, maxK = 20, seed = 1234, verbose = FALSE)
table(cluster_ids(sce, "meta20"))
```

**Figure 6 equivalent** -- median lineage-marker intensities across the 20
metaclusters. The paper's `plotClusterHeatmap()` was renamed to
`plotMultiHeatmap()`; the frequency bars come via `bars = TRUE`, and a
second (right-hand) heatmap needs `hm2` to be a character string
(`"abundances"`, `"state"`, or a marker name -- `NULL` is no longer valid):

```{r fig6, fig.height = 7}
plotMultiHeatmap(sce, hm1 = "type", hm2 = "abundances", k = "meta20",
    bars = TRUE, perc = TRUE)
```

**Figure 8/14-style** -- median lineage markers plus one signaling marker
(pS6), at the metacluster level and at the full 100-SOM-code level:

```{r fig8, fig.height = 7}
plotMultiHeatmap(sce, hm1 = "type", hm2 = "pS6", k = "meta20",
    bars = TRUE, perc = TRUE)
```

```{r fig14, fig.height = 9}
plotMultiHeatmap(sce, hm1 = "type", hm2 = "pS6", k = "som100", m = "meta20",
    row_anno = FALSE, bars = TRUE, perc = TRUE)
```

```{r plotClusterExprs, fig.height = 7}
plotClusterExprs(sce, k = "meta20", features = "type")
```

**Figure 13 equivalent** -- the 100 SOM codes themselves, colored by
metacluster:

```{r fig13}
plotCodes(sce, k = "meta20")
```

## Dimensionality reduction (UMAP)

```{r rundr}
set.seed(1234)
sce <- runDR(sce, dr = "UMAP", cells = 1e3, features = "type")
```

**Figure 9 equivalent** -- UMAP colored by CD4 expression:

```{r fig9}
plotDR(sce, "UMAP", color_by = "CD4")
```

**Figure 10/11 equivalent** -- UMAP colored by metacluster, overall and
stratified by sample:

```{r fig10}
plotDR(sce, "UMAP", color_by = "meta20")
```

```{r fig11, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 9}
plotDR(sce, "UMAP", color_by = "meta20") +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap("sample_id") +
    ggplot2::guides(color = ggplot2::guide_legend(ncol = 2,
        override.aes = list(size = 3)))
```

**"Percent cell class of the whole population, by condition"** -- stratified
by condition instead of by sample, i.e. the relative composition of the two
experimental groups on the same embedding:

```{r fig12}
plotDR(sce, "UMAP", color_by = "meta20") +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap("condition") +
    ggplot2::guides(color = ggplot2::guide_legend(ncol = 2,
        override.aes = list(size = 3)))
```

## Cluster merging

The paper manually annotates the 20 metaclusters into 8 known PBMC
populations (CD4/CD8 T-cells, B-cells IgM+/-, NK cells, monocytes, DCs,
surface-negative) using an expert-curated merging table
(`mergeClusters()`). That step requires visual inspection of the heatmap
above and biological knowledge of this specific panel; rather than guess
plausible-looking labels, this vignette uses `CATALYST`'s own automatic
`meta8` metaclustering (computed for free as part of `cluster()`'s
`maxK = 20` sweep) directly, and encourages readers reproducing this on
their own panel to do the manual `mergeClusters()` step described in the
paper (Figures 15-19) instead.

## Differential cell population abundance

**Figure 20/21 equivalent:**

```{r fig20}
plotAbundances(sce, k = "meta8", by = "sample_id")
```

```{r fig21, fig.height = 6}
plotAbundances(sce, k = "meta8", by = "cluster_id", shape_by = "patient_id")
```

**Figure 22 equivalent** -- `diffcyt`'s GLMM-based differential-abundance
test, with an observation-level random effect on `sample_id` to account for
overdispersion in the proportions (exactly as in the paper):

```{r da-test}
ei <- metadata(sce)$experiment_info
da_formula <- createFormula(ei, cols_fixed = "condition",
    cols_random = "sample_id")
contrast <- createContrast(c(0, 1))
da_res <- diffcyt(sce, formula = da_formula, contrast = contrast,
    analysis_type = "DA", method_DA = "diffcyt-DA-GLMM",
    clustering_to_use = "meta8", verbose = FALSE)
table(rowData(da_res$res)$p_adj < 0.05)
diffcyt::topTable(da_res, show_props = TRUE, format_vals = TRUE, digits = 2)
```

```{r fig22, fig.height = 5}
## plotDiffHeatmap()'s arguments changed too: 'th' -> 'fdr', 'hm1' removed,
## and 'y' must be the extracted rowData(), not the full diffcyt() result.
plotDiffHeatmap(sce, rowData(da_res$res), fdr = 0.05, normalize = TRUE)
```

## Differential marker expression (signaling markers)

**Figure 23/25 equivalent** -- median signaling-marker expression per
cluster and per sample:

```{r fig25, fig.height = 4}
plotPbExprs(sce[state_markers(sce), ], k = "meta8", facet_by = "antigen",
    shape_by = "patient_id")
```

**Figure 24 equivalent** -- `diffcyt`'s LMM-based differential-state test.
**Important:** unlike the DA test above, the DS test must *not* use
`sample_id` as a random effect (each cluster-sample combination already
contributes exactly one median value, so a `sample_id` random intercept is
perfectly confounded with the residual and the model fit silently returns
`NA` p-values for every row -- found empirically while writing this
vignette). Use `patient_id` (to account for the paired design, matching the
paper) or no random effect at all:

```{r ds-test}
ds_formula <- createFormula(ei, cols_fixed = "condition",
    cols_random = "patient_id")
ds_res <- diffcyt(sce, formula = ds_formula, contrast = contrast,
    analysis_type = "DS", method_DS = "diffcyt-DS-LMM",
    clustering_to_use = "meta8", verbose = FALSE)
table(rowData(ds_res$res)$p_adj < 0.05)
diffcyt::topTable(ds_res, top_n = 5, order_by = "p_adj",
    show_meds = TRUE, format_vals = TRUE, digits = 3)
```

```{r fig24, fig.height = 8}
plotDiffHeatmap(sce, rowData(ds_res$res), top_n = 30, all = FALSE,
    fdr = 0.05, normalize = TRUE)
```

## From CATALYST to CySA

CySA's SOM-based inputs (`SOM_codes`, `SOM_stats`, `map$colsUsed`) can be
built directly from this exact clustering -- the same FlowSOM run used for
every figure above, not a second, independently seeded run -- so the CySA
app and the CATALYST reference plots describe the identical clustering.

```{r cysa-inputs}
markers <- type_markers(sce)
cid <- as.integer(cluster_ids(sce, "som100"))
n_nodes <- nlevels(cluster_ids(sce, "som100"))

## Per-node (SOM code) marker medians, from the same clustering as above.
expr_t <- t(assay(sce, "exprs")[markers, ])
som_codes <- apply(expr_t, 2, function(v) {
    tapply(v, factor(cid, levels = seq_len(n_nodes)), median)
})
som_codes[is.na(som_codes)] <- 0

cysa_sce <- SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(exprs = assay(sce, "exprs")[markers, ]),
    colData = DataFrame(
        sample_id = factor(sce$sample_id),
        cluster_id = factor(cid, levels = seq_len(n_nodes))
    ),
    metadata = list(
        SOM_codes = som_codes,
        SOM_stats = data.frame(
            id = seq_len(n_nodes),
            n = as.numeric(table(factor(cid, levels = seq_len(n_nodes)))),
            mean = 0, median = 0, rdQu = 0, max = 0
        ),
        map = list(colsUsed = markers),
        experiment_info = as.data.frame(metadata(sce)$experiment_info)
    )
)
rownames(cysa_sce) <- markers
colnames(cysa_sce) <- paste0("cell", seq_len(ncol(cysa_sce)))

## A dList is required explicitly since there are only 10 (< 12) markers.
.pairD <- function(markers) {
    n <- length(markers)
    pairs <- list()
    k <- 1
    for (i in seq_len(n - 1)) {
        for (j in seq(i + 1, n)) {
            pairs[[paste0("d", k)]] <- c(markers[i], markers[j])
            k <- k + 1
        }
    }
    pairs[seq_len(min(6, length(pairs)))]
}

prepped <- prepClusterSelectorData(cysa_sce, total_cells_to_sample = 5000,
    dList = .pairD(markers), seed = 1234)
dend <- stats::as.dendrogram(
    stats::hclust(stats::dist(som_codes), method = "ward.D2")
)
dendTable <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_nodes), label = as.character(seq_len(n_nodes)))
clusterPatientTable <- table(
    sample_id = colData(cysa_sce)$sample_id,
    cluster_id = colData(cysa_sce)$cluster_id
)
somRasterData <- data.frame(
    x = rep(seq_len(10), 10), y = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10),
    id = seq_len(100)
)
for (m in markers) somRasterData[[m]] <- som_codes[, m]

app <- clusterSelector(
    sce = prepped$sce, sce_subsampled = prepped$sce_subsampled,
    dList = prepped$dList, dend = dend, dendTable = dendTable,
    clusterPatientTable = clusterPatientTable,
    somRasterData = somRasterData, somRasterObj = NULL
)
if (interactive()) shiny::runApp(app)
```

CySA's marker ridge, SOM raster heatmap and stats panels are then the
interactive counterparts of the static `plotMultiHeatmap()`/`plotAbundances()`
figures above, computed on the identical 100-node clustering.

## Technical comparison: with vs. without cyCombine

This particular dataset (Bodenmiller BCR-XL) has **no real technical batch**
-- all 16 samples were acquired in the same CyTOF run; `patient_id` is a
biological pairing variable, not a technical batch, and "correcting" across
patients would remove real biological signal, not a technical artifact. The
comparison below therefore only demonstrates the mechanics of
`cyCombine::batch_correct()` (treating patient as a stand-in batch purely
for illustration); it is **not** a recommendation to batch-correct this kind
of paired design.

```{r cycombine, eval = FALSE}
library(cyCombine)
sce_bc <- sce
colData(sce_bc)$batch <- colData(sce_bc)$patient_id
sce_bc <- batch_correct(sce_bc, markers = type_markers(sce_bc),
    covar = "condition", xdim = 8, ydim = 8, seed = 473)
```

Running this: `batch_correct()` completes and adds a `"cyCombine"` assay,
but reports *"Adjusting for 0 covariate(s)"* even with `covar = "condition"`
supplied -- i.e. in this cyCombine version the biological condition does not
appear to be protected from the correction as intended. Given that this
dataset has no real batch to correct in the first place, we do not pursue
this further here; anyone using `cyCombine` on a dataset with genuine
technical batches should verify with a positive control that `covar`/
`anchor` are actually preserving the biological signal of interest before
trusting the corrected output.

## Note on flowVS

An alternative to the fixed cofactor-5 arcsinh transform is `flowVS`, which
estimates a per-channel cofactor by optimizing a bimodality (Bartlett)
statistic. Trying this on the same 24 CyTOF channels:

```{r flowvs, eval = FALSE}
library(flowVS)
res <- estParamFlowVS(fs, channels = panel$channel_name[
    panel$marker_class %in% c("type", "state")
])
```

For roughly a third of the signaling ("state") channels, the per-channel
search returns `Bartlett's stat = MAX (10^9)` across almost the entire
candidate cofactor range (0.4 to > 20000) -- i.e. the optimizer cannot find
any interior optimum -- and the whole call eventually errors out with
*"missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"* before finishing all channels.
This matches the sparse, largely unimodal (single peak near zero) marker
distributions typical of CyTOF signaling channels, which don't have the
clearly bimodal negative/positive population structure flowVS's optimizer
was designed around for conventional fluorescence flow cytometry. This is
consistent with the standard CyTOF practice (and this workflow's own
default) of using a single fixed cofactor of 5 for all channels rather than
per-channel optimization.
